author: Shereen Siewert
title: Plea deal ends homicide case in Wausau overdose death; Schofield woman sentenced - NewsBreak
text:
By Shereen Siewert ,
8 hours ago Marisa Arne, 29, of Fond du Lac. June 17, 2025: First degree reckless homicide by delivery of drugs, bail jumping WAUSAU, Wis. — A Schofield woman was sentenced to six years in prison last week for providing the drugs that killed a 30-year-old Wausau man, closing a homicide case that had been set for a five-day jury trial beginning Monday.
Marisa M. Arne, 31, pleaded no contest Aug. 13 to first-degree reckless homicide by delivery of drugs and one count of felony bail jumping, according to Marathon County court records. Circuit Judge Suzanne O’Neill accepted the pleas, found Arne guilty and imposed sentence the same day. The hearing was scheduled Aug. 6, when the parties appeared for a jury status conference days before trial was to begin.
O’Neill ordered six years of initial confinement followed by 10 years of extended supervision, split across the two counts and served consecutively. Arne received credit for 409 days already served and was found eligible for the state’s Substance Abuse Program and Challenge Incarceration Program, either of which can shorten the confinement portion of a Wisconsin sentence.
The homicide count, a Class B felony, carries a maximum of 60 years. Arne was sentenced to 10 years on that count — three years confined, seven on supervision. On the bail jumping count, a Class H felony, she received the statutory maximum of six years, split evenly between confinement and supervision.
As part of the agreement, prosecutors dismissed and read in a second felony bail jumping count in the homicide case, along with all charges in three other pending Marathon County cases: two 2024 cases charging possession of narcotic drugs and three counts of felony bail jumping, and a 2025 case charging possession of narcotic drugs, possession of a controlled substance and possession of drug paraphernalia. Read-in charges are not separately punished but may be considered by the judge at sentencing.
Assistant District Attorney Sidney Brubacher prosecuted the case. Arne was represented by attorney Edmund Jelinski.
Arne has been in custody since shortly after her June 2025 arrest. Department of Corrections records show she was sent to Taycheedah Correctional Institution in Fond du Lac on Aug. 25, 2025 as a probation violator and released from that sentence March 17, 2026. She returned then to the Marathon County Jail pending trial.
The case stems from a June 11, 2025 call to a home on Wausau’s northwest side, where police and rescue crews found a man without a pulse and not breathing. He was taken to a local hospital and died four days later, according to a criminal complaint.
Investigators alleged the man bought drugs from Arne in a downtown Wausau parking lot, injected them and returned home, where he was found unresponsive on a bathroom floor. An autopsy detected fentanyl, gabapentin and other substances in his system, along with evidence of recent heart attacks, court documents state. The man had recently completed a 28-day rehabilitation program.
Arne was ordered to have no contact with the victim’s family unless authorized by the Department of Corrections, to maintain absolute sobriety and to complete assessment and treatment as recommended. She owes $921 in court costs and was ordered to provide a DNA sample.
Wisconsin’s “Len Bias” law allows a homicide charge when the delivery of a controlled substance results in another person’s death.
